messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
Project brief: Target is about 2,400 m. Total flight under 200 s because the range gives us short windows. We want dual deploy on this one. Provide the design and expected performance.

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: apogee is about 2,400 m, so the band is 2400 * 0.95 = 2280 m to 2400 * 1.05 = 2520 m. Total flight time has to be under 200 s. Dual deploy is required: a drogue at apogee and a main lower down. Landing speed is not stated, so I assume 6 m/s on the main. Rail and wind are not stated. I assume a 1.5 m rail, 2 m/s wind, vertical, sea level, one stage.
2. Feasibility: 2,400 m with no drag is sqrt(2 * 9.81 * 2400) = 217 m/s. A single chute at 5 m/s from that height takes 2400 / 5 = 480 s, which blows the 200 s window, so the drogue has to do most of the descent. A K motor on a 54 mm rocket is the class to check.

2. Feasibility: J350W is only 669 N*s, too small. K550W is 1,625 N*s and would sit high of 2,400 m on a 60 mm rocket. K400C is 1,307 N*s, 410 N, 54 mm, 0.359 m long, 1.19 kg, propellant 0.493 kg, with a 14 s delay. I'll plug it. The drogue opens at apogee and the main at 250 m, so the long descent is fast and the landing is still slow.
3. Size: guessed liftoff mass 1.8 kg, descent mass about 1.8 - 0.49 = 1.3 kg. Thrust-to-weight is 410 / (1.8 * 9.81) = 23. A drogue near 18 m/s needs 2 * 1.3 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 18^2) = 0.080 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 0.080 / 3.1416) = 0.32 m. I'll fit a 0.35 m drogue. The main, aimed at 5 m/s, needs 2 * 1.3 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 5^2) = 1.04 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 1.04 / 3.1416) = 1.15 m. I'll fit a 1.2 m main. From 2,400 m the drogue covers most of the 200 s budget and the main only has 250 m left.
4. Draft: 60 mm fiberglass body, 0.95 m long, ogive nose, three plywood fins, 54 mm mount, AeroTech K400C. Defaults: 1.5 m rail, 2 m/s wind.
